To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
solar radiation, wind and cable line direction can affect the power cable current-carrying capability.
the current-carrying capability of a power cable depends on the solar radiation, the cable’s line direction and the wind direction, as well as the cable’s line inclination.

(1) The current-carrying capability of power cables is influenced by wind and solar radiation, (2) The impact of wind on current-carry-ing capacity of power cables depends on wind direction, (3) The impact of solar radiation on current-carry capacity of power cables is dependent on geographical direction of the power cables line.
In summary, our research is concerned with
evaluation of current-carying capacity of power cable installed in free air and taking into account the impact of solar irradiance, wind direction and geographical line direction.

the following issues: (i) determination of the current-carrying capability of power cables in the free air, (ii) determination of the impact of solar irradiance, wind and geographical direction on the current-carryng capability of the cables, (iii) development of a method for determining the current-carry capacity of power cables, (iv) determination of the temperature distribution along the length of the power cables.

the following issues: 1) selection of appropriate numerical model for calculation of current-carry-ing capacity of power cables in free air, 2) determination of impact of solar radiation on power cables current-carring capacity in free air, and 3) determination of impact on power cables current- carrying capacity of wind and power cable line direction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current-carrying power cable capacity is affected by the wind direction, the cable geographical direction and solar radiation.
CFD simulations should be performed to assess current-carrying capability of cables, especially when they are installed in free air and the cable line is not located in the direction of wind.
the impact of solar and wind effects on power cables current-caring capacity should be taken into account in the design of the power cables.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CFD simulations should be used for the evaluation of power cables current-carring capacity.
the impact of solar and wind conditions should be taken into account during selection of cross-sectional areas of power cables conductors.
the CFD simulations of the cable current-carrying capability in free air are a valuable and reliable tool in the design of electrical power networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current-carrying capacities of power cables are affected by the solar radiation and wind direction.
the current-carrying capacities of the cables installed on the roof of the building, in the open air, in the tunnel and in the cable duct are different.
the current-carrying power capacity of power cables is dependent not only on the cable’s conductor cross-section area, but also on the cable installation conditions.
